# FDG8100

> DO ensure that `Object.Equals` and the equality operators have exactly the same semantics and similar performance characteristics.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.13 Equality Operators.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1046
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

CA1046 reports an externally visible reference type that overloads operator == without overriding Equals (probe with SDK 10.0.402: a type that also overrides Equals was not reported, and immutable types were); then Equals keeps reference equality while the operator does not, which is the case of the body (Object.Equals needs to be overridden). The C# compiler also warns about it (CS0660). Whether the two have the same semantics and similar performance is not checked, so coverage is partial. CA1046's message suggests removing the operator rather than overriding Equals, and it has no code fix.

## From the book

This often means that `Object.Equals` needs to be overridden when the equality operators are overloaded.

```csharp
public struct PositiveInt32 : IEquatable<PositiveInt32> {
  public bool Equals(PositiveInt32 other) { ... }
  public override bool Equals(object obj) { ... }
  public static bool operator==(PositiveInt32 x, PositiveInt32 y){
    return x.Equals(y);
  }
  public static bool operator!=(PositiveInt32 x, PositiveInt32 y){
    return !x.Equals(y);
  }
  ...
}
```
